metadata.title: Terraform Docs, Quoted
metadata.author: Varnika M
metadata.voice_reason: Varnika chose a computer voice on 2026-10-11, then asked to reuse her Week 01 voice, Kokoro am_onyx. The toolkit also uses am_onyx for the instructor's 'Liam, in for Bear' narrator; this film uses only the stock voice, with no Liam name, greeting, or @NikBearBrown outro.
metadata.bookend_exempt_reason: The hesitant writer, terms card and Your Turn composer carry the instructor's narrator and channel identity, which this student film may not show (assignment: narrate as yourself; no instructor name, persona or credit line). B01 is the hook. BOUT is kept, drawn in Manim with the film title and Varnika's name.
metadata.constructed_rule: Drawings of anything that does not exist yet carry a 'planned' label. Real docs lines carry a source tag. B07A and B07B redraw Varnika's real 2026-10-11 screenshots and say 'redrawn'; the screenshots themselves are in evidence/alternatives/.
metadata.claude_output_rule: B07B summarises one real claude.ai reply (Sonnet 5.5, 2026-10-11), redrawn and dated on screen. No other Claude reply is shown.

beats.narration_text: I'm Varnika. My final project will be a tool that answers questions about Terraform from the official docs, and proves every answer with the exact line it came from.

beats.narration_text: Here's a real example. You might guess that an S3 bucket's name is required. The AWS provider docs say it's optional: if you leave it out, Terraform picks a random, unique name.

beats.question: 1 · How it will work
beats.narration_text: It will work in three steps. Find the docs lines that match the question. Ask Claude to answer using only those lines, and to quote one. Then my code checks that the quote really exists in the docs before showing the answer.

beats.question: 4 · What it proves
beats.narration_text: It's meant to show what this course teaches: a prompt contract, where Claude must reply in a fixed shape with an answer, a quote and a line number; source grounding; verification in code; and an evaluation that lists every miss. It won't prove the tool works on all of Terraform, only on the questions I test.

beats.question: 5 · In, out, first
beats.narration_text: It covers about ten AWS resource pages at one pinned version. It will not write or run Terraform, and it never touches a cloud account. The first piece is the quote checker, and you'll know it runs when its tests pass offline, including one where a made-up quote is rejected.

beats.question: 6 · Risk
beats.narration_text: The risk I can already see: on the same page, bucket is optional at the top, but required inside the replication block. A search for the word bucket could pick the wrong line, and the quote would still be real. So I'll track which section every line belongs to, and put this exact case in my tests.
